item.title: Beyond API Compatibility: Building a Tool to Measure the Blast Radius of Library Changes
item.description: Quasar can then connect the library API to its consumer across repositories.Language-specific indexers emit SCIP definitions, references, and relationships into Quasar’s shared semantic graph.Relationships are especially useful when generated code separates the API a producer owns from the symbols consumers invoke For example, Quasar can trace a Protobuf definition through its generated Java members to the repositories that use them, even when consumer code never names the .proto element.SCIP records symbols and their references; it does not determine whether an API change violates an ecosystem’s compatibility rules Producers can review change findings through Quasar’s REST and GraphQL APIs or its MCP server, then investigate affected repositories and call sites

item.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
item.description: Naive byte-range caching can waste gigabytes of origin bandwidth on small requests We rebuilt our cache architecture in Pingora to coordinate partial fetches automatically, cutting R2 p99 latency in half.

item.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
item.description: Cloudflare's new post-quantum GeoKey Manager protects geographically fenced decryption keys from harvest now, decrypt later attacks Learn how we redesigned our cryptography stack to support strict data sovereignty in a post-quantum world.
